tiebreaker.q: In what year was the very first Academy Awards ceremony held?

questions.q: In Disney's 1989 animated film “The Little Mermaid”, what is the mermaid's name?
What kind of animal is the title character of the 1942 Disney film “Bambi”?
Which 1993 comedy has a television weatherman living the same day over and over in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania?
In the 2010 animated film “Despicable Me”, what are the small yellow henchmen called?
Which 1997 film starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet is set aboard a doomed ocean liner?
In which 1976 film does the hero train by running up the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art?
In Marvel's 2018 film “Black Panther”, what is the name of the fictional African nation that T'Challa rules?
In the 1965 musical “The Sound of Music”, what is the surname of the Austrian family whose seven children are taught to sing?
In the 1952 musical “Singin' in the Rain”, Gene Kelly's character dances through a downpour while swinging around what piece of street furniture?
Which 1927 film starring Al Jolson is generally credited as the first feature-length film with synchronised spoken dialogue?
In the 1995 film “Apollo 13”, how does the crew's most famous line finish: “Houston, we have …”?
questions.a: “… a problem” (the real 1970 transmission was “Houston, we've had a problem”)

questions.q: In the 2003 animated film “Finding Nemo”, what three words does Dory sing to keep herself going?
In the 1996 film “Jerry Maguire”, what four-word demand does the football player shout down the phone at his agent?
In the 1984 film “The Karate Kid”, what four-word instruction does Mr. Miyagi give Daniel while he polishes the cars?
“You'll believe a man can fly” was the tagline of which 1978 superhero film?
In the 2001 film “The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring”, what does Gandalf roar at the creature on the bridge?
In the 1989 film “Field of Dreams”, the whispered voice in the cornfield says “If you build it …” — what comes next?
questions.a: “… he will come” (accept “they will come”, the way the line is usually misquoted)

questions.q: “In space, no one can hear you scream” was the tagline of which 1979 science-fiction film?
Which 1939 epic ends with Rhett Butler telling Scarlett O'Hara “Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn”?
Which 1959 Billy Wilder comedy ends with the line “Well, nobody's perfect”?
Which actor voiced the Genie in Disney's 1992 animated film “Aladdin”?
Which actor played James Bond in the 1962 film “Dr. No”?
Which actress played the title role in the 1964 Disney musical “Mary Poppins”?
Which Canadian-born actor starred in “Ace Ventura: Pet Detective”, “The Mask” and “The Truman Show”?
Which writer-director made the 1980s teen films “The Breakfast Club” and “Ferris Bueller's Day Off”?
Which actress starred in “Roman Holiday” in 1953 and “Breakfast at Tiffany's” in 1961?
Which actor played the lawyer Atticus Finch in the 1962 film “To Kill a Mockingbird”?
Which Japanese director co-founded Studio Ghibli and made “My Neighbour Totoro” and “Spirited Away”?
Which actress was the first Black woman to win the Academy Award for Best Actress?
Which director was the first woman to win the Academy Award for Best Director, for the film “The Hurt Locker”?
In the “Star Wars” saga, which 1980 film is Episode V?
The seven “Harry Potter” novels were adapted into how many feature films?
questions.a: Eight (8) — the last book was split into two films

questions.q: In the 1989 film “Back to the Future Part II”, Marty McFly travels forward to which year?
Which film and cartoon franchise features four crime-fighting turtles named after Renaissance artists?
Which 2008 film starring Robert Downey Jr. was the first release in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
In the “Pirates of the Caribbean” films, what is the name of Captain Jack Sparrow's ship?
In the “Indiana Jones” films, what is Indiana Jones's day job when he is not off hunting relics?
In the original 1968 “Planet of the Apes”, the closing scene reveals the ruined remains of which New York landmark?
Which Japanese screen monster first appeared in a 1954 film and has been followed by dozens of sequels since?
In the “Pink Panther” film series, what is the name of the bumbling French detective played by Peter Sellers?
“Bollywood” is the nickname for the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, India.
On a film set, a “boom” is a long pole used to hold a microphone above the actors, just out of shot.
A “director's cut” is the version of a film that has been re-edited to the studio's requirements.
Silent films were normally shown in complete silence, with no music playing in the theatre.
In the 1933 film “King Kong”, the giant ape makes his last stand on top of the Empire State Building.
The Hollywood sign in Los Angeles originally read “Hollywoodland”.
The word “blockbuster” was first used to describe a hugely successful film.
Every film that has ever won the Academy Award for Best Picture has been in the English language.
Walt Disney's “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” was the first full-length animated feature film produced in the United States.
Film trailers are called trailers because they were originally shown before the main feature.
